title: Prospective, Randomized, and Controlled Study of a Human Umbilical Cord Mesenchymal Stem Cell Injection for Treating Diabetic Foot Ulcers
protocol: Recruit patients with ages between 18 years and 80 years.
Ensure patients have type 2 diabetes meeting WHO diagnostic criteria from 1999.
Confirm HbA1c level ≤10% in patients during screening or within 3 months prior to randomization.
Verify ankle-brachial index of at least 0.8 without intermittent claudication.
Select foot ulcers graded 1 or 2 according to the Wagner grading system.
Ensure ulcers are located on the foot, ankle, or front shin.
Confirm cross-sectional area after debridement is between 2-5 cm².
Ensure no visible pus or necrotic substance for at least 4 weeks before randomization.
Exclude patients undergoing routine treatment of other wounds.
Select the wound with the most severe grade if two or more wounds are similarly large.
If there are two or more wounds with the same area and grade, select the one with the longest duration.
Ensure patients sign an informed consent form before participating in the clinical study.
Disinfect the wound locally with povidone-iodine in the stem cell therapy group.
Remove necrotic tissue from the wound surface using surgical scissors.
Aspirate 50 mL of physiological saline into a syringe to clean the wound surface thoroughly.
Measure the wound area using the sterile foil edge hook method.
Apply the sterile film transparent dressing with its coordinate grid to the wound surface.
Outline the shape of the wound along its edge with a marker.
Calculate the wound area according to the area of each coordinate grid on the film.
Inject human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (2 x 10^5 cells/cm²; 0.4 mL/cm²) into the periphery and base of the wound.
Trim the sterile dressing to an appropriate size.
Cover the trimmed sterile dressing over the wound surface.
Bandage the wound after covering it with the sterile dressing.
Disinfect the wound locally with iodophor.
Remove necrotic tissue from the wound surface using surgical scissors.
Aspirate 50 mL of physiological saline and clean the wound surface inside and out.
Measure the wound area using the sterile foil edge hook method.
Apply a sterile film transparent dressing with its coordinate grid to the wound surface.
Outline the shape of the wound along its edge with a marker.
Calculate the wound area according to the area of each coordinate grid on the film.
Trim the silver ion dressing to an appropriate size.
Cover the trimmed silver ion dressing over the wound surface.
Bandage the wound after covering it with the silver ion dressing.
Obtain demographic data of subjects.
Record concomitant treatments.
Record wound status, including location, area, depth, infection, and ischemia.
Record wound healing rate.
Record healing time.
Record complications.
Perform laboratory tests.
Take wound secretion for swabs and bacteriological culture.
Conduct routine blood tests.
Test liver function.
Test kidney function.
Examine patients on the first day of therapy.
Conduct follow-up visits 15 days after last therapy.
Conduct follow-up visits 30 days after last therapy.
Record treatment effects during follow-ups.
Record condition changes during follow-ups.
Record recovery situation during follow-ups.
Record current living status during follow-ups.
Calculate primary outcome index: The 30 day wound healing rate = (original wound area − unhealed wound area at 30 days)/original wound area × 100%.
Calculate secondary outcome index: Wound healing time.
Define the time of wound closure as the time at which the wound is completely re-epithelialized.
Calculate complete healing rate: The complete healing rate = the number of complete healed cases/the total number of cases × 100%.
Calculate the surgical intervention rate using the number of surgical interventions divided by the total number of cases multiplied by 100%.
Record subjects undergoing debridement and drainage, skin grafting, adjacent skin flap, distal skin flap, non-anastomotic skin flap, or amputation as patients with surgical interventions.
Perform bacterial culture according to standard clinical inspection procedures.
Calculate the pathogen positive rate using the number of cases detected pathogen positive divided by the total number of cases multiplied by 100%.
In case of an adverse event during stem cell clinical research, take necessary treatment and rescue measures.
Track and investigate all adverse events and their treatment process.
Record results in detail until properly resolved or until the condition is stable.
Follow up on any abnormal test with clinical significance until it returns to normal.
